parsed.main_gap: The proof never establishes that g cannot take negative values, so the reduction V⊆{0,c} is unjustified as written.

errors.description: At most one positive value does not imply every value is 0 or c. One must exclude g(x)=d<0; iterating (4) would give g(x+nd)=d and positivity of all x+nd, an eventual contradiction.
errors.quote:
Consequently, either

* (i) $g\equiv 0$ (constant), which gives $f(x)=x$, a solution; or  
* (ii) there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.

errors.description: The case g≡c>0 is omitted from the stated dichotomy. It is already a completed solution and should be separated from the mixed case where both 0 and c occur.
errors.quote: there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.

errors.description: For x∈S0 and y∈Sc, the displayed expansion of A(x,y) has 4cy, not 4cx. This term is unused, so the typo does not affect the subsequent argument.

parsed.notes: The missing negativity argument and omitted constant-positive branch are both short, direct repairs. Apart from these issues and the harmless typo, the functional equation, separation, covering argument, and verification are sound.
